title: Suspect Arrested after Stolen Vehicle Burned on Cedar Hill Golf Course
content:
26-9930
On May 27, 2026, at approximately 9:00 p.m., the Saanich Police Department received a report of a stolen vehicle from a residence in the 600 block of Jolly Place.
A short time later, officers located the vehicle in the parking lot of the Cedar Hill Recreation Centre and attempted to stop it. The driver fled onto the Cedar Hill Golf Course, contacting two police vehicles in the process. Officers did not pursue and instead established containment around the golf course.
With maintaining containment, an officer observed a fire on the golf course. Upon investigating, they located the stolen vehicle burning in the middle of a fairway. The Integrated Canine Service was requested and, shortly after beginning a track, the suspect was located in a nearby bush and arrested.
Saanich Fire attended and extinguished the fire.
The driver remains in custody pending a court appearance. Investigators anticipate recommending charges related to the theft and burning of the vehicle as well as the damage to Cedar Hill Golf Course and fleeing from police.

title: Witnesses and Dashcam Footage Sought in Suspicious Vehicle Fires
content:
On May 23, 2026, at approximately 12:30 a.m., the Saanich Police Department responded to a report of a vehicle fire in the 3200 block of Glasgow Avenue.
Upon arrival, officers found two vehicles engulfed in flames and contained the area to allow Saanich Fire to extinguish them.
Officers from our Forensic Identification Section attended to document the scene, and detectives from our Major Crime Unit continue to investigate.
The fires are considered suspicious.
Anyone who witnessed the incident or was travelling in the area at the time and has dashcam footage is asked to contact our non-emergency line at 250-475-4321 and reference file 26-9569.

title: Saanich Police Seize Suspected Fentanyl, Cocaine, and Methamphetamine in Drug Trafficking Investigation
content:
26-7327
On Friday, May 15, 2026, the Saanich Police Department’s Patrol Division, with support from the Street Crime Unit (SCU), the Greater Victoria Emergency Response Team, the Integrated Canine Service and the Forensic Identification Section, executed a search warrant at a residence in the 400 block of Dupplin Road in relation to a drug trafficking investigation. At the same time, a search warrant was executed at a storage locker linked to the investigation.
The warrants were executed following extensive proactive policing by Patrol Division officers in the Midtown area, with support from the SCU.
The search resulted in the seizure of approximately three kilograms of what is believed to be fentanyl, cocaine and methamphetamine, along with 10 litres of GHB. The estimated street value of the drugs is approximately $55,000.
A significant amount of stolen property was also recovered, including heat pumps, air conditioners, generators and lawn mowers, valued at approximately $25,000. The rightful owner has been identified, and the items will be returned.
Two individuals were arrested at the time and later released. Patrol officers and the SCU continue to investigate and anticipate recommending several drug trafficking related charges to Crown counsel.

title: Guilty Plea Entered in Unprecedented Voyeurism Case Involving 652 Victims
content:
A 39-year-old Saanich man has pleaded guilty in what is believed to be the most prolific case of voyeurism ever prosecuted in Canada, after investigators identified 652 individual women and girls as victims.
On January 16, 2024, the Saanich Police Special Investigation Section (SIS), with the assistance of the British Columbia Integrated Child Exploitation Unit, began a voyeurism investigation after a SIS detective was made aware of voyeuristic photos and videos being uploaded to a popular image-based social media site from somewhere in Saanich.
The investigation led detectives to identify Yin Yeung Derek Chan as a suspect. Chan was previously convicted of voyeurism after being caught filming a woman in a mall change room in the Capital Region.
On April 11, 2024, Chan was arrested at his Saanich home. During the execution of a search warrant, detectives seized devices containing thousands of images and over 28 hours of offending video that were recorded between April 1, 2017, and Nov. 30, 2023, without the knowledge or consent of women and girls inside businesses, at beaches, and in a few instances, through the windows of private residences across the region.
Following a thorough review of the evidence seized, investigators determined that 652 separate women and girls were captured in the photos and videos, and that Chan had been posting the imagery online. Detectives noted that many of the images were posted to and viewed on websites around the world, and formal requests were made to have them removed.
Chan was released with conditions following his initial arrest in April 2024 and was rearrested on January 30, 2025. He was detained by the court and has remained in custody since then.
On October 1, 2025, Yin Yeung Derek Chan pleaded guilty to several criminal offences related to voyeurism, including surreptitiously recording people in a place where they reasonably expect privacy, observing and recording for a sexual purpose, making child pornography, publishing a recording that was obtained in the commission of a crime, and breaching three separate conditions, two of which related to his previous conviction.
Of the 652 women and girls, detectives were able to formally identify and contact 40 victims, some of whom delivered victim impact statements for sentencing.
Chan is scheduled to be sentenced on May 21, 2026, at Victoria Law Courts.
SIS detectives continue to work to formally identify all the women and girls in this case. Anyone who believes they may be one of the hundreds of unidentified victims is asked to email:
[email protected]
.
Greater Victoria Victim Services has been assisting many of the identified victims and are available to provide support to anyone who comes forward.

title: Search Warrant Executed at Illegal Gaming House as part of Joint Investigation
content:
In early 2026, the Saanich Police Department began an investigation into the operation of an illegal gaming house. The investigation is being led by the department’s Street Crime Unit, in partnership with the Drug and Organized Crime section of the RCMP’s Federal Policing Pacific Region.
The suspected location of the illegal gaming house was within the Victoria Police Department’s jurisdiction. VicPD was consulted early in the investigation, and it was agreed that SPD’s Street Crime Unit would lead the file.
On April 23, 2026, at 10:30 p.m., a search warrant was executed at a business in the 400-block of Burnside Road East. Several individuals were arrested, and approximately $12,000 in currency, along with gambling equipment and related paraphernalia, was seized.
The operation was supported by the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of BC’s Joint Illegal Gaming Enforcement Team, the Greater Victoria Emergency Response Team, Victoria Police Remote Piloted Aerial Support Unit, SPD Patrol officers, the Special Investigation Section and Forensic Identification Services.
The investigation remains ongoing. At this time, charges have not been recommended to Crown counsel; however, investigators anticipate recommending charges related to the operation of an illegal gaming house at a later date.
Quotes:
“This investigation reflects the strength of collaboration between local, regional and federal policing partners,” said Drew Robertson, officer in charge of the Saanich Police Department’s Detective Division. “Bringing together specialized resources and expertise across agencies was critical in executing this search warrant. We are particularly grateful to CFSEU-BC’s Joint Illegal Gaming Enforcement Team for their specialized knowledge of illegal gaming investigations and their support in advancing this complex, cross-jurisdictional investigation.”
“Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of BC’s (CFSEU-BC) Joint Illegal Gaming Enforcement Team (JIGIT) brings specialized expertise and a province-wide intelligence lens to complex investigations like this one,” said S/Sgt. Alvin Ng. “By working alongside Saanich Police and our Federal Policing Pacific Region partners, we are able to disrupt organized illegal gaming operations that often intersect with broader criminal activity. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to protecting communities by targeting illicit networks and holding those responsible accountable.”

title: Saanich Police Launch Online Reporting
content:
The Saanich Police Department has launched an online reporting system that gives residents a new way to report select non‑urgent incidents.
Online reporting allows the public to submit reports for certain incidents at a time that is convenient for them, which supports more timely reporting of incidents that may otherwise go unreported. This also improves the efficiency of police service delivery and helps reduce wait times for the public.
The system is available through the Saanich Police Department website and includes clear instructions and examples to help users determine whether their incident is suitable for online reporting. This option is intended to complement, not replace, reporting by phone or in person.
Online reporting should not be used for emergencies, crimes in progress, or incidents requiring immediate police attendance. In those situations, the public should call 911 or the police non‑emergency line.
The online reporting system is now available at
www.saanichpolice.ca
under Services and Reporting.
The development of the web resource to host the online reporting system was fully funded through the Government of BC’s C-STEP program.

title: Remembering Constable Robert Kirby | April 24th
content:
April 24, 2026, marks the 66th
anniversary of the murder of 31-year-old Saanich Police Constable Robert (Bob) Norman Barrie Kirby.  He remains the only Saanich Police Officer to have been killed in the line of duty during our department’s 120 years of service.
On April 24th, 1960, a 44-year-old psychiatric patient escaped from the Colquitz Provincial Mental Hospital on Wilkinson Road.  This location is now home to the Vancouver Island Regional Correctional Centre. The escapee quickly broke into a nearby resident’s shed, where he stole two .22 calibre rifles, then fired upon some of the unarmed hospital staff.
Constable Robert Norman Barry Kirby, “Barry” to his family and “Bob” to his co-workers, was working at the front desk at the time of the escape. He immediately joined other Saanich Police officers and responded to the Wilkinson Road area.
Soon after he arrived, Constable Kirby formed up with Police Corporal Bob Coleman as one of several search teams.  A short time later, Constable Kirby was ambushed and shot in the chest by the escapee, who was hiding in some bushes about 15 feet away.  This was at a property on Markham Street. The rifle round split the top button of Constable Kirby’s tunic in two and then pierced his heart, killing him instantly.  Corporal Coleman returned fire immediately, but the escapee was not hit, and he fled into a wooded area just off Viaduct Avenue.
About 40 minutes later, the escapee was still at large when he opened fire again, shooting an unarmed psychiatric nurse in the shoulder.  Fortunately, the nurse was able to survive his injuries.
Moments later, Constable Walter Mycock shot and immobilized the escapee.  He was quickly arrested, but he would never stand trial due to his mental state.  The escapee was later recommitted to a different institution.
At the time of his murder, Constable Kirby was a nine-year police veteran who had served seven years with the St. Boniface and Winnipeg Police Services and served as a Saanich Police officer for two years. He was also a veteran of the Royal Canadian Navy.
Constable Kirby was survived by his wife Dorothy and their four young children – three-week-old Shaun, three-year-old Candace, six-year-old James, and nine-year-old Robert.
The following District of Saanich Archives link is an online photo gallery which contains several pages of photos from Constable Kirby’s funeral procession in downtown Victoria and from his graveside service at Royal Oak Burial Park:
https://saanich.accesstomemory.org/
On Friday, April 25th, 2026, Saanich Police officers attended the Royal Oak Burial Park at Constable Kirby’s grave to lay wreaths and remember him by way of a brief service.
We will always remember and honour Constable Kirby for making the ultimate sacrifice to keep his community of Saanich safe.

title: Vehicles Impounded for Street Racing thanks to Dashcam Footage
content:
On February 12, 2026, just after 11 a.m., two vehicles were captured on dashcam footage weaving in and out of traffic in the 4100 block of Quadra Street.
The person who recorded the footage contacted Saanich Police and provided the video to a member of the Traffic Safety Unit (TSU) for investigation.
After reviewing the footage, the TSU officer determined the two vehicles were street racing and that their actions endangered other road users. Because the licence plates were clearly visible, the officer was able to identify the registered owners of both vehicles.
When spoken to by police, neither vehicle owner identified who was driving at the time of the incident. As a result, both vehicles were impounded for seven days for street racing, and each owner received tickets for driving without due care and attention and for failing to provide driver information.
This incident demonstrates how dash camera footage can assist police in investigating and deterring dangerous driving. If your camera captures unsafe driving behaviour, please report it to police. Your information can help hold those who put others at risk accountable and contribute to safer roads in Saanich.

title: Saanich Police Target Shoplifting Through Enforcement and Business Outreach
content:
The Saanich Police Department noted an increase in shoplifting incidents across the district. In response, officers conducted Operation Hidden Costs throughout February, an enforcement initiative involving both covert and uniform operations at four major retail locations in Saanich.
The operation led to the recovery of more than $1,000 in stolen property belonging to local businesses, including a large volume of consumable goods and other retail items. Thirteen individuals were arrested, resulting in six criminal charges.
“Shoplifting causes real harm to businesses, whether they are large retailers or small, locally owned shops,” said Inspector Andy Stuart, Officer in Charge of Patrol. “Our department recognizes that impact and remains focused on addressing it.”
Operation Hidden Costs was funded through a C-STEP grant provided by the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General.
As part of the same C-STEP grant funding, the Saanich Police Department is hosting a series of information sessions for business operators focused on shoplifting. The first session has already taken place and was well attended. A second session is scheduled for March 26.

title: Major Crime Unit Investigates Bank Robbery
content:
On March 18, 2026, at 1:45 p.m., Saanich Police received a report of a robbery at a bank in the 300 block of Burnside Road West.
The suspect entered the bank, approached a teller, and produced a note demanding money. The suspect fled with an undisclosed amount of cash.
The suspect was tracked to a building in the 3600 block of Tillicum Road. Officers responded to the area, located the suspect, and arrested them shortly after 2:15 p.m. They remain in custody.
The Saanich Police Department’s Major Crime Unit has assumed conduct of the investigation.
Victim Services has been engaged to support bank employees affected by the incident.

title: Temporary Deployment of CCTV Camera | July 1
content:
The Saanich Police Department will deploy a temporary camera at the Gorge Canada Day Picnic along the Gorge Waterway in support of our operations to help ensure public safety during the event. The camera will be clearly visible and mounted on our Command Vehicle, operating in a public space in accordance with provincial and federal privacy laws. It will be removed at the conclusion of the event.
“The use of a CCTV camera will help us monitor Canada Day celebrations responsibly and support a timely response if needed,” said Deputy Chief Damian Kowalewich. “Our focus is on creating a safe, family-friendly environment where the community can come together and celebrate.”

title: Man Charged Following Serious Assault in Gorge Park
content:
On July 11, 2026, Saanich Police patrol officers responded to reports of an alleged assault in Gorge Park near the Craigflower Bridge.
Responding officers located a male victim suffering from significant but non-life-threatening injuries. He was transported to hospital for medical treatment.
During the investigation, a portion of Gorge Park was closed to allow officers to conduct a thorough examination of the scene.
On July 14, Kyle Dustin David Aird was arrested. He has since been charged with one count of aggravated assault and two counts of breaching court-ordered conditions. He remains in custody pending a bail hearing.

title: Repeated Vandalism and Theft Targeting Speed Reduction Signs Under Investigation
content:
The Saanich Police Department is investigating repeated acts of vandalism and theft targeting speed reduction signs in the 4200, 4300 and 4400 blocks of Torquay Drive.
Since April 29, 2026, there have been 10 incidents in which signs have been damaged or stolen. The most recent incident occurred on July 13.
Anyone who witnessed these incidents, noticed suspicious activity near these signs, or has information that may assist our investigation is asked to call the Saanich Police non-emergency line at 250-475-4321 and note that they are calling regarding file 26-8715.

title: Additional Victims Sought in June 4 Assault Investigation
content:

title: Witnesses and Dashcam Footage Sought in Cyclist Collision
content:
On July 27, just before 5:30 p.m., the Saanich Police were contacted by BC Emergency Health Services who had responded to an injured cyclist in the road at the intersection of Parkside Crescent and Winchester Road. Paramedics advised that they believe the cyclist may have collided with or been hit by a vehicle that was no longer at the scene when they arrived.
Patrol officers responded to the scene and began investigating.
The cyclist was transported to hospital with serious injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening injuries.
Anyone who was travelling in the area at the time and witnessed a collision involving the cyclist, or has dashcam footage from the area, is asked to contact our non-emergency line at 250-475-4321 and reference file 26-14460.

title: Saanich Police Launch Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems Program
content:
The Saanich Police Department has launched a Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) program, adding drone technology to support frontline policing. The program is designed to enhance officer and public safety while improving situational awareness during critical incidents. The aircraft provide officers with a safe aerial perspective during incidents, helping them assess evolving situations, search large areas, and gather real-time information to support operational decisions.
The RPAS program will support officers in a range of policing functions, including:
Critical incident response
Missing person investigations
Crime scene management
Public event management
Emergency disaster response
Training
Only trained and certified SPD pilots/officers will be operating the drones. All flights will be carried out in accordance with privacy legislation, federal aviation requirements, Transport Canada guidelines, and departmental policy.
A drone does not replace responding officers. It provides additional information that may assist officers and other emergency responders on the ground. Our RPAS program reflects our commitment to adopting technology that supports effective policing and helps us better serve our community.

title: Saanich Police Investigate Fatal Collision
content:
Saanich Police are investigating a collision between a commercial vehicle and a pedestrian that occurred on August 8, just after 3 A.M. at the intersection of McKenzie Avenue and Glanford Avenue.
Despite the efforts of first responders at the scene, the pedestrian succumbed to their injuries. Next of kin have been notified.
The driver of the commercial vehicle stayed at the scene and is cooperating with investigators.
The area was closed for several hour to allow our forensic investigators and collision analysts to gather evidence. The investigation is now being conducted by the Saanich Police Major Crime Unit.
